title: Hartlepool's Seaton Tandoori crowned Britain's best at Curry Life Awards
excerpt: The Seaton Carew restaurant has taken the top national prize — Best Restaurant of the Year — at the Curry Life Awards 2026, outshining curry houses from across the country.
body:
• Seaton Tandoori in Seaton Carew, Hartlepool, has been named Best Restaurant of the Year at the Curry Life Awards 2026.
  • The national awards, organised by Curry Life Media Group, honour the best of Britain's curry industry, with ceremonies drawing restaurateurs, MPs and industry leaders.
  • The restaurant holds a 5-out-of-5 food hygiene rating from Hartlepool Council and averages 4.4 out of 5 across more than 1,500 online reviews.
  • Find it at 31 The Front, Seaton Carew, Hartlepool TS25 1BS (01429 890101); it opens evenings seven days a week.

A Hartlepool Indian restaurant has been crowned the best in the country. Seaton Tandoori, on The Front in Seaton Carew, took the title of Best Restaurant of the Year at the Curry Life Awards 2026, the national ceremony celebrating Britain's curry industry.

The win was announced at the awards' gala ceremony, where the restaurant's team collected a framed plaque bearing the Best Restaurant of the Year 2026 title. The Curry Life Awards are organised by Curry Life Media Group and contested by Indian restaurants from across the UK, making the top prize one of the most sought-after honours in the sector.

A national stage for curry

The Curry Life Awards have grown into a major fixture of Britain's hospitality calendar. The event brings together leading restaurateurs, suppliers, politicians and media to recognise excellence across the curry industry, from neighbourhood takeaways to destination dining rooms, and is often described as a national celebration of the country's curry restaurants.

Previous editions have drawn high-profile backing. Cobra Beer, founded by Lord Karan Bilimoria, has headlined as sponsor, and past ceremonies have been attended by MPs. The awards span categories covering the country's best restaurants, chefs and takeaways, with winners chosen from across the industry.

"The UK's curry industry features some of the country's most innovative entrepreneurs and restaurateurs. All of them have inspiring stories to tell, and they must be given the necessary support to grow and thrive."

— Syed Belal Ahmed, Editor, Curry Life Media Group

Last year's Best Restaurant of the Year title went to Jamun, an Indian street-food restaurant in Brighton, underlining how the top prize has recently rewarded ambitious regional restaurants outside London.

The Seaton Carew winner

Seaton Tandoori sits on The Front in Seaton Carew, the seaside district of Hartlepool, serving classic Indian restaurant dishes alongside tandoori grills, thalis and set meals for groups. Review aggregators put its rating at 4.4 out of 5 from more than 1,500 reviews across Just Eat, Facebook and other platforms, with diners praising its service, generous portions and consistency.

The restaurant also holds the top 5-out-of-5 food hygiene rating from Hartlepool Council, awarded after an inspection in May 2026. In an industry where trust is earned plate by plate, a clean inspection record and a loyal local following count for a great deal with judges.

For a town better known for its maritime history and its football club than its dining scene, a national restaurant title is a notable coup. Hartlepool's independent hospitality businesses have been working to raise the town's profile, and a best-in-Britain award gives Seaton Tandoori — and the town — a calling card few competitors can match.

Diaspora angle

The win is fresh evidence of how deeply South Asian hospitality is woven into Britain's food culture. Indian restaurants, many of them family-run businesses built up over decades, remain among the most decorated parts of the UK hospitality industry, and national awards like these keep that contribution — and the communities behind it — in the spotlight.

What's next

National titles tend to bring fuller dining rooms. Seaton Tandoori opens evenings seven days a week, and the award is likely to draw diners from well beyond Hartlepool in the coming months. For the industry's ambitious regional restaurants, the message of this year's result is simple: the top prize is anyone's to win.
